reliabilityRules.primary: The organisation that measured or legislated the figure, publishing it itself: manufacturer technical data sheets, government standards and regulations, nutrition labels, peer-reviewed primary research, standards bodies.
reliabilityRules.secondary: Competent parties reporting or synthesising others' measurements: review papers, extension services, trade associations, club guides, practitioner reference tools.
reliabilityRules.tertiary: General reference works. Useful orientation, never adequate to support a numeric specification in this project.

citationRules.numericClaim: A record carrying numeric specifications must cite at least one source with reliability primary or secondary AND deepLink true. A tertiary source, or a bare publisher homepage, can never support a number.
citationRules.qualitativeClaim: Descriptive text may rest on any source, including tertiary, provided the source is named.
citationRules.verification: full-text means the document was retrieved and the figures read out of it. metadata-only means the document's existence and title were confirmed but the figures were taken from a search summary or abstract. unverified means neither — the citation is inherited from earlier work and has not been checked.

sources.title: Brewing Sour and Wild Ales (incl. 'The Falcon Method For Fermenting Lambics', credited to MB Raines)
sources.supports: Brettanomyces species characters — B. claussenii/anomalus (English stock beer origin, softer, pineapple and mango), B. bruxellensis (Brussels, medium earthy funk), B. lambicus (every lambic, huge horsey character with fruitiness, smoky and sour). Lactobacillus delbrueckii: lactic acid for crisp dry acidity, primary character of Berliner Weisse, ferment very warm e.g. 98 °F. Pediococcus: large lactic production from glucose, no CO2, massive diacetyl charge in early ferment. Acetobacter as 'vinegar mother' converting ethanol to acetic acid. Enterobacter contributing bilious characters. Timeline: at least a month before cultures show character, optimally six months to a year. Named blends WLP655, Wyeast 3278, Wyeast 3763 Roeselare.
sources.doesNotSupport: Temperature ranges, attenuation, flocculation or alcohol tolerance for any of these organisms except the single 98 °F figure for L. delbrueckii.

sources.title: 125th Anniversary Review: Bacteria in brewing — the good, the bad and the ugly
sources.publisher: Journal of the Institute of Brewing 118:335-345
sources.supports: Lactobacillus brevis and Pediococcus damnosus as the lactic acid bacteria most commonly implicated in beer spoilage; L. brevis among the most hop-tolerant; hop iso-alpha-acids as ionophores impairing proton motive force; beer typically carrying 17-55 ppm iso-alpha-acids as an intrinsic antimicrobial hurdle.
sources.doesNotSupport: Species-level temperature ranges, alcohol tolerances or per-species IBU inhibition thresholds. Figures here were read from abstract and search summaries, not the full text — verification is metadata-only.

sources.title: WildBrew Philly Sour — Technical Data Sheet
sources.supports: Lachancea thermotolerans, pure active dried strain; attenuation 74-82%; 20-30 °C (68-86 °F), optimal 25-30 °C (77-86 °F); flocculation high; alcohol tolerance 9% ABV; pitching 50-150 g/hL; viability >=1x10^9 CFU/g; POF negative; diastaticus negative; killer negative; aroma sour, red apple, stone fruit, peach; fermentation completable in 10 days at 20 °C.
sources.doesNotSupport: Species-wide behaviour of L. thermotolerans outside this product; titratable acidity figures are quoted in Lallemand standard-conditions wort only.

sources.title: The yeast Kluyveromyces marxianus and its biotechnological potential
sources.supports: Lactose assimilation and fermentation; thermotolerance with maximum growth temperature variously reported as 47 °C (Anderson et al. 1986), 49 °C (Hughes et al. 1984) and 52 °C (Banat et al. 1992); ethanol production above 40 °C; LOWER ethanol tolerance than S. cerevisiae, correlated with plasma-membrane ATPase activity (Rosa & Sá-Correia 1992); Crabtree-negative and facultatively fermentative; cannot grow under strictly anaerobic conditions, with ethanol formation almost exclusively linked to oxygen availability.
sources.doesNotSupport: Any single numeric alcohol tolerance for the species. The 10% v/v figure circulating for K. marxianus comes from strains after ~100 days of directed adaptive evolution and is not a native specification.
